Hi Satoshi — thanks for the heads up and for including Claire.

Short answer: yes, we see this occasionally when Calendly's auto-detect picks the browser locale (or the browser reports a different timezone because of VPNs or corporate policy). Two pragmatic workarounds that have worked for customers across APAC/EU:

- Use the timezone dropdown inside the Calendly page (top-right). Manually set it to the timezone you want (JST) and then pick the slot.
- If Calendly still behaves oddly, use our Chili Piper link (included below) — it tends to respect the calendar account timezone when the user is signed into Google/Outlook.

If both of those fail, I'll send a one-click calendar invite from my side. To avoid back-and-forth, here are two candidate slots in your window (all shown as JST):
- Tue 2026-05-25 09:30 JST / Mon 24 23:30 CEST (Claire)
- Wed 2026-05-26 10:00 JST / Wed 26 02:00 CEST (Claire) — this one is tight for Claire so prefer the first

If either works, reply with preferred slot and I'll send the invite (with Zoom). I attached a very short mutual action plan so we can align the agenda if you confirm.
